## Start and stop

| Do this | To |
| --- | --- |
| `cd` into your project folder, then `claude` | Start a session in that folder. Claude can read and change files there. |
| `claude --version` | Check it's installed |
| `claude doctor` | Check your install and settings when something's off |
| `/exit`, or {{< kbd Ctrl-D >}} twice | Leave the session |
| `claude --continue` | Pick up your last session in this folder |

## Keys

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| {{< kbd Esc >}} | Stop Claude mid-step, keeping the work so far, so you can redirect it |
| {{< kbd Esc >}} {{< kbd Esc >}} (empty input) | Open the rewind menu: go back to an earlier point |
| {{< kbd Shift-Tab >}} | Change the permission mode (see below). On Windows, if it does nothing: {{< kbd Alt-M >}} |
| {{< kbd Ctrl-V >}} (Mac Terminal), {{< kbd Cmd-V >}} (iTerm2), {{< kbd Alt-V >}} (Windows) | Paste a screenshot into your prompt |
| {{< kbd Ctrl-G >}} | Open the plan, or your prompt, in a text editor to edit it |
| {{< kbd Ctrl-O >}} | Show the full details of what Claude did |
| `!` at the start | Run a shell command yourself, such as `! open dashboard.html` |
| `@` | Point at a file, such as `@README.md` |

## Permission modes

The bottom of the screen shows the current mode. {{< kbd Shift-Tab >}} cycles through them.

| Mode | Claude… | Use it when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `⏵⏵ auto mode on` (the default) | Acts without asking; a separate safety check reviews each action and blocks risky ones | You trust the direction of the task |
| `⏸ manual mode on` | Asks before edits and most commands; reads freely | You want to see every step |
| `⏵⏵ accept edits on` | Edits files, and runs file commands like `mkdir`, `mv` and `rm` in the folder, without asking; asks before other commands | Edits are routine |
| `⏸ plan mode on` | Reads and proposes a plan, changes nothing | Anything that matters: read the plan first |

`/plan <what you want>` jumps straight into plan mode. When the plan is ready you choose **Yes, and use auto mode**,
**Yes, manually approve edits**, or **No, keep planning** (then type what to change).

## Commands we used

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/statusline <what to show>` | Choose what the line under the input box shows: model, folder, effort, context used. `/statusline remove it` turns it off |
| `/plan <task>` | Plan first, change nothing until you approve |
| `/goal <condition>` | Keep working until the condition is true; a separate model checks after each turn. Give it a finish line Claude can prove, and a limit like "stop after 5 turns" |
| `/memory` | See and edit what Claude remembers: your `CLAUDE.md` files and its own notes |
| `/init` | Draft a `CLAUDE.md` for this folder |
| `/rewind` | Go back to before a prompt: restore the files, the conversation, or both |
| `/clear` | Start a fresh conversation (memory files stay) |
| `/skills` | List the skills Claude can use here |
| `/reload-skills` | Pick up a skill you created or changed in a skills folder that's new this session |
| `/artifacts` | List pages you've published, and copy their links |
| `/usage` | See how much of your plan's usage you've used |
| `/context` | See how full the conversation is |
| `/btw <question>` | Ask a side question without derailing the work |
| `/help`, `/powerup` | Help, and short interactive lessons on features |
| `/doctor` | Diagnose and fix setup problems |

## Memory: two kinds

| | You write it | Claude writes it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **What** | `CLAUDE.md` in your project folder | Auto memory: notes Claude saves as it learns your project |
| **How** | Ask: *"Add this to CLAUDE.md: …"*, or run `/init` for a first draft | On by default; you'll see "Saved 1 memory" |
| **Where** | Your folder, next to your files | `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/` |
| **Good for** | Rules and facts Claude can't know: definitions, deadlines, house style | Things it figured out along the way |

Keep `CLAUDE.md` short. Every line is read at the start of every session.

## Skills (also called custom commands)

A skill is a folder with a `SKILL.md` file of instructions. It becomes a command named after the folder.

```text
.claude/skills/house-style/SKILL.md   →   /house-style
```

- **You** can run it by typing `/house-style`.
- **Claude** can also pick it up on its own when its description matches what you asked for.
- Put it in your project's `.claude/skills/` to keep it with the project, or in `~/.claude/skills/` to use it everywhere.
- The old `.claude/commands/name.md` files still work and do the same thing.

The easiest way to make one: ask Claude. *"Create a skill called … that …"*

## Habits worth keeping

1. **Plan before anything that matters.** Read the plan for assumptions you didn't make.
2. **Write down what it can't know**: definitions, dates, rules, all in `CLAUDE.md`.
3. **Give it a way to check its work**: a number you trust, a test, a screenshot, a `/goal`.
4. **Check one number yourself.** Looking right isn't being right.
5. **Know your undo.** `/rewind` restores Claude's file edits but not what shell commands did (deleting or moving
   files). Work on copies, and use git for anything real.
6. **Mind the data.** Only give it data you're allowed to share with an AI service, and follow NC State's rules for
   sensitive data.
7. **Start fresh between tasks** with `/clear`. Long, tangled sessions get worse, not better.
